gloss: to enrich (soil); to fatten (livestock); to line one's own pockets

definitions.explanation: To add nutrients to soil so that crops grow well. Used in agricultural contexts.
To raise the body weight of an animal, especially livestock, by feeding it well.

definitions.gloss: to line one's pockets; to enrich oneself (figurative)
definitions.explanation: Used in the idiom {私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やす to mean enriching oneself unfairly, usually through one's official position.

examples.japanese: {堆肥|たいひ}で{土|つち}を{肥|こ}やす。
examples.english: I enrich the soil with compost.

examples.japanese: ミミズが{土|つち}を{肥|こ}やしてくれる。
examples.english: Earthworms enrich the soil for us.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいねん}{秋|あき}に{落|お}ち{葉|ば}を{畑|はたけ}に{混|ま}ぜて{土|つち}を{肥|こ}やしている。
examples.english: Every autumn I mix fallen leaves into the field to enrich the soil.

examples.japanese: {牛|うし}を{肥|こ}やしてから{出荷|しゅっか}する。
examples.english: They fatten the cattle before shipping them.

examples.japanese: {農家|のうか}は{豚|ぶた}をよく{肥|こ}やしてから{市場|しじょう}に{出|だ}す。
examples.english: The farmer fattens up the pigs well before sending them to market.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}に{備|そな}えて{家畜|かちく}をしっかり{肥|こ}やすのが{昔|むかし}からの{知恵|ちえ}だった。
examples.english: Fattening livestock well in preparation for winter has been wisdom from ancient times.

examples.japanese: あの{政治家|せいじか}は{私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やしていた。
examples.english: That politician was lining his own pockets.

examples.japanese: {部下|ぶか}を{利用|りよう}して{私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やすやり{方|かた}は{許|ゆる}せない。
examples.english: I can't forgive the way he used his subordinates to enrich himself.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{公共|こうきょう}の{資金|しきん}で{私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やしていたとして{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: He was arrested for having lined his own pockets with public funds for many years.

notes:
Transitive godan verb ({五段|ごだん}, す-stem). Causative form of {肥|こ}える (to grow fat; for soil to become rich). The intransitive pair is {肥|こ}える.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Transitive: {土|つち}/{家畜|かちく}/{私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やす
- Intransitive pair: {肥|こ}える (to become rich/fat on its own)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土|つち}を{肥|こ}やす: to enrich the soil
- {家畜|かちく}を{肥|こ}やす: to fatten livestock
- {私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やす: to line one's own pockets (idiom, sense 3)
- {目|め}を{肥|こ}やす: to develop a discerning eye (figurative — gain experience by seeing many examples)

IDIOMS:
- {私腹|しふく}を{肥|こ}やす: literally "fatten one's private belly" — to abuse a position for personal gain.
- {目|め}を{肥|こ}やす: to refine one's eye through experience.

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {肥|こ}やしていませんでした
